<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, `@objectstack/service-messaging`, touching **25** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-messaging/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**3** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/email-templates.mdx`  _(via crm_deal (literal, a string literal in problemOf; a string literal in scalarParamProblem))_
- `content/docs/automation/hook-bodies.mdx`  _(via crm_deal (literal, a string literal in problemOf; a string literal in scalarParamProblem))_
- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`  _(via crm_deal (literal, a string literal in problemOf; a string literal in scalarParamProblem))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-messaging/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **8** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e491fce2c70a67a92f2c40cb38e2f8b23af40ce4` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b20e8609d59ef72f17e330dd2c9075a21c5333fa` — the merge of head `b487097576deb8a3ca437c89e3960908e289a24b` into base `e491fce2c70a67a92f2c40cb38e2f8b23af40ce4`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b20e8609d59ef72f17e330dd2c9075a21c5333fa && git checkout b20e8609d59ef72f17e330dd2c9075a21c5333fa
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e491fce2c70a67a92f2c40cb38e2f8b23af40ce4 b487097576deb8a3ca437c89e3960908e289a24b && git checkout -B drift-repro e491fce2c70a67a92f2c40cb38e2f8b23af40ce4 && git merge --no-ff b487097576deb8a3ca437c89e3960908e289a24b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e491fce2c70a67a92f2c40cb38e2f8b23af40ce4
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e491fce2c70a67a92f2c40cb38e2f8b23af40ce4` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `f48717397cb1245a471d87fe91c59c4d148cc96f`
Local-runs: none

Face: declaration (`Clause-② yes (widening)` alone; the tree touches no `packages/spec/src` and no governed path). Inputs: card #36853 and its comments, this PR's body and file list, the net diff against `main` (merge-base `fbcfdfbb5`, 8 files), and the 53 check-runs on the head (37 success, 16 skipped by path filter, none failed). Author login is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, so no extra author note.

### ① Derived judgments

- **J1 — accept set of `EmitInput.keyedText.params` widened by `{ list, separator }`: right, and it is a pure widening.** `problemOf` routes a plain object carrying `list` to `listParamProblem` and everything else to `scalarParamProblem` / `keyedParamProblem`, which are the old string / `{ object, fallback }` / `{ key, fallback }` checks moved verbatim. Only the text of one refusal changed. A row that passed before still passes. A `{ list }` object was refused before (an undeclared `list` member), so no stored row can change meaning. In the renderer, `scalar()` is the old per-param branch unchanged, including the once-per-render object-label translation. Every row stored before renders byte for byte as it did.
- **J2 — what an older reader does with a list row: degrades to the literal, never breaks.** On `main`'s reader, the same closed-shape `problemOf` sees `list` as an undeclared member of a keyed param. So `readNotificationTextKeys` returns `undefined` on both read paths (dispatcher claim and inbox read). The row is then delivered or served as its stored English literal, title and body alike. Nothing throws. Writer/reader version skew inside one install cannot happen in a supported setup: `@objectstack/service-messaging` and `@objectstack/plugin-approvals` sit in the same `fixed` changeset group, so they always release together. What remains is a rollback, and there the notice reads in English. That is safe but not stated anywhere (F2).
- **J3 — emit refusals: right.** Refused: an empty list, more than 100 items, an undeclared member on the list or an item, a separator that is not a well-formed `{ key, fallback }`, a non-object item (a sparse hole included), a bad item key, fallback or params name, a non-scalar item param, and a list nested in an item, which gets its own message. A stored malformed row reads back as `undefined` and is served as its literal. The new test pins every one of these, along with a stored row that reads back.
- **J4 — per-recipient isolation: holds.** `renderWith` builds `params`, the `scalar` closure, the lazily built `translation` and every item's `itemParams` fresh for each call. `renderAllFor` calls it once per recipient, in that recipient's negotiated locale. The list path adds no cache. The only renderer-wide state is still `announcedMisses`, which is log de-duplication only, and list items and the separator go through `lookup` / `lookupSeparator`, never `entry`. The params are the emit's own and are identical for every recipient. No recipient's locale or data reaches another's render.
- **J5 — `lookupSeparator` keeps a whitespace or punctuation answer (`', '`, `'、'`) and still treats an empty answer, an echoed key or a throw as a miss: right.** `lookup`'s `trim()` test would have thrown away the en `', '`. An item or separator that misses falls back alone. That is the existing per-param fallback rule, so a partial catalog can mix languages inside one list by design. The PR names this.
- **J6 — public surface: right.** New runtime export `NOTIFICATION_LIST_PARAM_MAX_ITEMS`. New type exports `NotificationScalarParam`, `NotificationListParam` and `NotificationListItem`. `NotificationTextParam` becomes `NotificationScalarParam | NotificationListParam`. The same union widens the read side: the exported channel contract `Notification.keyedText` can now carry a list param. In the repo, the only channel that reads it is the inbox, which stores it verbatim, and both readers validate through `readNotificationTextKeys`. The changeset names only the emit side (F3), and its list of exports leaves out the constant (F4).
- **J7 — plugin-approvals producer: right for slates up to 100 slots.** `noApproverNotice` sends 2+ slots as `approvalNoApproverHolding` with `who` set to the list. Each item is `approvalNoApproverSlot` with the existing `slotParams`, and its fallback is the English clause the row stores. The separator falls back to `enMessages.approvalNoApproverSlotSeparator`. The `interpolate` list branch builds the same literal `noApproverWho` builds, so the English body is unchanged. Every pack derives its `Slots2`–`Slots8` sentences as Holding with the clauses joined by that pack's separator, so a 2–8 slot notice renders the same text per pack as before. Keeping `Slots2`–`Slots8` in the packs is right: stored `keyedText` rows carry those keys and are rendered again at every inbox read. The mirror types `ApprovalScalarParam` / `ApprovalListParam` match the messaging shapes. The producer does not bound the list, though. Above 100 slots `emit()` refuses, `notify()` catches it and logs a warning, and the submitter gets no notice at all (F1).
- **J8 — card acceptance: met.** `admin-rescue-named-slate.integration.test.ts` opens a 9-slot slate through the real service and renders it through the real `NotificationTextRenderer` in zh-CN. The result is `岗位「销售经理」、团队「团队1」…部门「部门4」` with `not.toMatch(/[A-Za-z]/)`, and the `en` render equals the stored literal. CI is green on the head, all 10 Test Core shards included.

### ② Semver level

- `patch` for both packages is right under AGENTS.md (Post-Task Checklist 3): the level follows the Metadata-protocol kind, `none` takes `patch`, and a non-protocol widening ships `patch`. New exports and a widened accepted shape do not raise it to `minor` here.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` is right. `keyedText` is a service API, and no `packages/spec/src` schema or metadata type lets an author write it.
- The Clause-② declaration reads `yes (widening)`, line-initial, in both the PR body and the changeset. That is right: the accepted set grows, and no value accepted before is refused. Check Changeset is green.

### ③ Boundary flags

- PR "Small decisions" — Slots2–8 kept: agreed (J7). Item params scalar only: agreed. A nested list would need a second separator and a depth bound, and no producer needs one. Per-item and per-separator fallback: agreed (J5). The 100-item cap: agreed as a bound on the render cost of every read, but the plugin's producer must respect it (F1).
- PR "Owed — the seat rules whether a contract review is owed": answered. The `Clause-② yes` declaration alone makes this review owed at `TIER_DEFAULT`, and this record is it.
- SQL push-down: no finding. The diff adds no data read, no id materialisation and no in-app join.

#### Findings

- **F1 — should-fix.** `noApproverNotice` sends an unbounded list. A slate of more than `NOTIFICATION_LIST_PARAM_MAX_ITEMS` (100) literal slots is refused by `emit()`, swallowed by `notify()`'s catch, and the submitter gets no notice, where `main` would have sent the English-slot notice. Either cap the list in the producer (mirror the constant, the way the types are mirrored, and fall back to the `noApproverWho` text for a larger slate) or drop the cap's effect on this producer. Pin it with a test.
- **F2 — nit.** The PR body and changeset do not say what a reader on an older version does with a list row. It drops the whole `keyedText` and serves the English literal, title included (J2). One sentence in the changeset would cover a rollback.
- **F3 — nit.** The changeset names only `EmitInput.keyedText.params`. The same widening reaches the exported read side, `Notification.keyedText`, which a third-party channel may read and narrow (J6).
- **F4 — nit.** The changeset's list of new exports leaves out `NOTIFICATION_LIST_PARAM_MAX_ITEMS`. The PR body lists it.

No must-fix. F1 is should-fix, so landing waits until a delta closes it and this reviewer reads that delta. F2–F4 may go into the same delta or be accepted as written.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-axt9gn`
Reviewed-by: `session_01L6bhgV6i8jfWwSXjpWJrjA`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Final head after the contract review

Head-sha: `b487097576deb8a3ca437c89e3960908e289a24b` (one commit after `f48717397`)

This commit carries what contract review 7204071400 asked for:

- **F1:** `noApproverNotice` sends the list param only for 2 to `APPROVAL_LIST_PARAM_MAX_ITEMS` (100) slots. `APPROVAL_LIST_PARAM_MAX_ITEMS` is a new constant in plugin-approvals that mirrors `NOTIFICATION_LIST_PARAM_MAX_ITEMS`. A larger slate rides `approvalNoApproverHolding` with `who` set to the English clauses joined, which is what `main` sends past 8 slots. The emit is therefore not refused, and the submitter is still told.
- **Pin:** a new test in `admin-rescue-named-slate.integration.test.ts`.
  - It asserts that the two constants are equal.
  - It runs a 101-slot slate through `assertNotificationTextKeys`. The check passes and `who` is the English string.
  - It runs a 100-slot slate the same way. The check passes, the list has 100 items, and the zh-CN render contains no English type.
  - Without the fix, the pin fails with `holds 101 items (at most 100)`.
- **F2, F3, F4:** added to the changeset. F2 covers what an older reader does with a list row after a rollback (it falls back to the whole English literal). F3 covers the widened read side, `Notification.keyedText`. F4 adds `NOTIFICATION_LIST_PARAM_MAX_ITEMS` to the list of new exports.

CI on this head: 53 check-runs, all success or skipped by path filter, none failed.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `b487097576deb8a3ca437c89e3960908e289a24b`
Local-runs: none

Delta round 2 on the declaration face, after record 7204071400 at `f48717397`. Inputs: card #36853 and its comments, this PR's body and file list, the full delta `f48717397..b48709757` (1 commit, 4 files), the net diff against `main` (merge-base `fbcfdfbb5`, the same 8 files; still no `packages/spec/src` path and no governed path, so the face stays declaration), PR comment 7204574135, and the 53 check-runs on the head (37 success, 16 skipped by path filter, none failed or pending). The author login is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, so there is no extra author note.

### ① Derived judgments

- **J9 — the 101-slot fallback reaches the submitter: yes, and no refusal path is left.** `noApproverNotice` sends the list only for `slots.length > 1 && slots.length <= APPROVAL_LIST_PARAM_MAX_ITEMS`. A larger slate falls through to `noApproverWho(note.slots, declaredLabel)`, with no `render`, so it is the English clauses joined by `', '`. That string rides as the scalar `who` of `approvalNoApproverHolding`. `emit()` checks `keyedText` with `assertNotificationTextKeys` (messaging-service.ts:1367), and that function caps only a list's item count. A string param has no length cap, so the notice passes. `slots.length` counts the slots after `slotsOf` filters the slate, and that is the same array `slotList` would map, so the count the guard checks is the count the list would hold. For a slate over 100 the branch is byte for byte what `main` sends for any slate over 8, so nothing regresses. The new test opens 101 and 100 slots through the real service. It runs the emitted `keyedText` through the same `assertNotificationTextKeys` that `emit()` uses (the emit in the test is a stub, so the check is called directly), and it checks both `who` and the stored body. The 101 case would have thrown `holds 101 items (at most 100)` on the old head.
- **J10 — the mirrored constant against drift: safe as pinned.** `plugin-approvals` lists `@objectstack/service-messaging` only under `devDependencies`. Importing the constant would add a runtime dependency that the plugin does not have today. So mirroring it follows the precedent the PR already set for the list types. The pin `expect(APPROVAL_LIST_PARAM_MAX_ITEMS).toBe(NOTIFICATION_LIST_PARAM_MAX_ITEMS)` sits in the plugin's integration suite. Both packages are in the same workspace, so a change to the messaging cap in either direction fails that pin in CI before it lands. The two packages also release together. `APPROVAL_LIST_PARAM_MAX_ITEMS` cannot be reached from the plugin's only entry point (`exports["."]` → `index.ts`, which does not re-export `approval-notification-text`), so it is not public surface.
- **J11 — English over 100, rather than the list cut with a count: acceptable, recorded as an accepted deviation.** The fallback is `main`'s own behaviour, and the changeset now says so. A cut list with "and N more" would need a new sentence in every pack. It would also drop slot names from a notice whose job is to name what an administrator must staff, and the stored English literal is the audit text. A slate of more than 100 unresolved `type:value` literals on one step is outside any real configuration. The card's acceptance (9 slots, zh-CN, no Latin) is still met, and the 100-slot case stays a list. One limit: the 100-slot zh-CN assertion is `not.toMatch(/team/)`, which is weaker than the 9-slot `/[A-Za-z]/`, because the test values `t0`…`t99` are Latin. It still proves that the type word is translated, which is the point.
- **J1–J8 of 7204071400 stand.** The delta touches neither `notification-text.ts` nor `index.ts`, and the accept set, refusals, renderer isolation and public surface of `service-messaging` are unchanged.

### ② Semver level

- `patch` for both packages still holds. `Metadata-protocol: none`, and the delta adds no public export: the new constant cannot be reached from the plugin's entry point.
- Clause-②: `yes (widening)`. It stays line-initial in both the PR body and the changeset, and it is still right: the accepted set of `keyedText.params` grows and no value accepted before is refused. The delta narrows what the plugin produces, not what the messaging service accepts. Check Changeset is green.
- **F2 — closed.** The changeset now states that an older reader, after a rollback, serves the whole notice, title and body, as its English literal, and that nothing fails.
- **F3 — closed.** The changeset now names the read side, `NotificationTextParam` → `Notification.keyedText`, and warns channel readers.
- **F4 — closed.** The changeset's list of exports now includes `NOTIFICATION_LIST_PARAM_MAX_ITEMS`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **F1 — closed.** It is fixed as asked: the producer caps the list at a mirrored constant, a larger slate falls back to `noApproverWho`'s text, and it is pinned at 101 and 100 slots with the constants pinned equal (J9, J10).
- The PR's "Small decisions" and "Owed" were answered in 7204071400 and still hold. The 100-item cap is now respected by its only producer.
- SQL push-down: no finding. The delta adds no data read, no id materialisation and no in-app join.

#### Findings

- **F5 — nit.** Two lines still say the list covers every slate. The changeset's summary line ends "names a slate of any size in the reader's language", which becomes the CHANGELOG headline. The PR body's plugin-approvals bullet says `noApproverNotice` spells "a slate of two or more slots" as the list param. Above 100 slots neither is true now. The changeset's own last bullet states the exception, so this is wording only. It may be fixed on the prose face or accepted as written.

No must-fix and no should-fix remain, so this is the final round. Accepted deviations: J11 (English clauses above 100 slots, as on `main`) and F5 if it is left as written.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-axt9gn`
Reviewed-by: `session_01L6bhgV6i8jfWwSXjpWJrjA`

**VERDICT: PASS**

**L1 checklist**
- **Shape and relation.** `l1-face.mjs --pr 37701` on this head; all 53 check-runs success or path-filter skip, none failed. Eight files across `service-messaging` and `plugin-approvals`, both at `patch` in one changeset.
